Abstract
Background
Research demonstrates significant gender- and sexual orientation–based differences in orgasm rates from sexual intercourse; however, this “orgasm gap” has not been studied with respect to age.
Aim
The study sought to examine age-related disparities in orgasm rates from sexual intercourse by gender and sexual orientation.
Methods
A survey sample of 24 752 adults from the United States, ranging in age from 18 to 100 years. Data were collected across 8 cross-sectional surveys between 2015 and 2023.
Outcomes
Participants reported their average rate of orgasm during sexual intercourse, from 0% to 100%.
Results
Orgasm rate was associated with age but with minimal effect size. In all age groups, men reported higher rates of orgasm than did women. Men’s orgasm rates ranged from 70% to 85%, while women’s ranged from 46% to 58%. Men reported orgasm rates between 22% and 30% higher than women’s rates. Sexual orientation impacted orgasm rates by gender but not uniformly across age groups.
Clinical Translation
The persistence of the orgasm gap across ages necessitates a tailored approach in clinical practice and education, focusing on inclusive sexual health discussions, addressing the unique challenges of sexual minorities and aging, and emphasizing mutual satisfaction to promote sexual well-being for all.
Strengths and Limitations
This study is the first to examine the orgasm gap with respect to age, and does so in a large, diverse sample. Findings are limited by methodology, including single-item assessments of orgasm and a sample of single adults.
Conclusion
This study revealed enduring disparities in orgasm rates from sexual intercourse, likely resulting from many factors, including sociocultural norms and inadequate sex education.
Keywords: orgasm, aging, orgasm gap, sexual orientation, gender differences
Orgasm is a psychophysiological response to sexual stimulation involving muscle contractions, hormonal changes, and tension release. 1 While not essential for sexual pleasure, 2 , 3 orgasms are frequently sought in both solitary and partnered sexual activity, contributing to sexual satisfaction and well-being. 4-8 The absence of orgasm can cause distress and relationship challenges. 9-11 In sexual intercourse, orgasm rates vary across genders and sexual orientations, with women—particularly heterosexual women—reporting lower orgasm rates than men and lesbian women (ie, the orgasm gap). 12-14 Prior investigations into these disparities have revealed a complex interplay of biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors influencing sexual pleasure. However, the impact of age on the orgasm gap is unexplored. Studying age in this context can uncover developmental influences on sexual health, offering insights for interventions that enhance sexual functioning across the lifespan. This study assessed differences in orgasm rates from sexual intercourse by gender, sexual orientation, and age.

hn.title: Gaussian Splats part 3: There's always a bigger scene
hn.text:
Gaussian splats part 3: There’s always a bigger scene
22 Sept
Written By Sam Birley
Previously, on OKO…
The year was 2025, and as I wrote last time , the industry had fallen head over heels for Gaussian splats, and Magnopus right along with it. I'd spent a good while dragging our Unreal splat renderer out of Niagara and rebuilding it around the engine's instanced rendering: every splat registered as an instance, a GPU-side sort on each frame was invoked to composite the transparency in the right order, and a material shaded each one into a soft ellipse.
It worked, and it worked well enough that I wrote a whole article about it. I felt rather pleased with myself.
Well, as it turns out, I celebrated way too soon when I claimed a capability of rendering unlimited splats. In reality, several walls were making this categorically untrue, and the first one was much closer than I expected.
Not so unlimited after all…
The first wall
Here's a humbling thing I only learned after publishing that last article: the renderer I'd been showing off had a hard cap of about 16 million splats per asset . I hadn't the faintest idea. Every asset I'd tested happened to sit under it, but the limitation was always there. In my hubris, I just didn’t know about it yet.
That limit came down to where the per-splat data actually lived. Registering every splat as a modern mesh instance in Unreal meant handing it to the engine's GPU Scene , effectively a central ledger of typically everything in the world that resides on the GPU.
And while GPU Scene is superb at what it does, it was built to support thousands of instances of a mesh – not tens of millions or hundreds of millions – under the hood is a cap of at most 16 million instances of a given mesh. When you cross it, things come apart; only part of the asset is visible at any given time, graphical corruptions abound, and you get a warning printed on the viewport informing you of your failure.
The naive solution, and the one that worked out for me, was to stop using the GPU Scene to track splats altogether. Instead, I went fully old-school and relied on a more traditional instance-render pipeline that more or less ended up being a direct invocation of what’s generally known as DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect.
This required a few key steps:
Skip registering instances with the GPU scene; do a classic indirect instanced draw instead.
Feed the indirect draw buffer the draw count from the sort keygen shader, which was already iterating over all splats while generating sort keys per-frame.
Store all splat instance data on the GPU via textures (which we also got for free from the last article ).
Write a small vertex factory (Unreal's abstraction over vertex shaders and their material bindings) and have the vertex shader sample the sorted splat buffers (see the last article), get the appropriate splat attributes and then pass that onto the material.
The rendered image came out pixel-for-pixel identical to before, but the 16-million ceiling evaporated, because the thing imposing it was no longer in the loop. Our test asset of ~30 million splats was rendering happily. Better!
Free from the shackles of GPU Scene’s max instance count.
Some other nice things fell out of the custom vertex factory approach too. Since splat meshes are always trivial quads, they’re easy to derive procedurally in the shader itself, which meant there was no longer a need to specify an actual Unreal mesh – the system just derives the vertex attributes in the vertex shader, making the whole thing a little more turnkey.
And the other benefits that indirect-instanced-draw effectively moved us to more of a bindless-rendering approach.
Since we were already iterating over all splats each frame while generating their sort keys, we could also do more advanced per-splat culling in there, and then write the sum total of all visible splats to the indirect draw buffer. We now only drew exactly the number of splats visible within the camera frustum, and the culling logic lived entirely on the GPU.
Before – GPU Scene implementation
After – indirect instanced draws and per-splat culling
While that’s great, in that it gives us a nice performance boost, what’s also worth calling out is that the number of splats being drawn per frame was now truly variable , and decided entirely on the GPU. The pipeline had grown into the right kind of shape a level-of-detail system needs; drawing a different subset every frame, decided at the last possible moment.
I hadn’t set out to build an on-ramp to LODs. But that’s what it turned out to be.
Hubris: Redux
Lifting that instance cap felt like the finish line. However, in less than a week I hit the next wall.
Because the GPU Scene exfiltration had changed how many splats I could draw , but not how many I could hold : every splat in the scene still lived in GPU memory, all the time. That's completely fine when the whole scene fits. But obviously a splat isn't free in terms of memory. Position, scale, orientation, opacity, spherical harmonic coefficients, all told about 32 bytes per-splat once I'd packed it as tightly as I dared.
Which implies you can throw a lot of splats at VRAM, until you meet a real photogrammetry capture of a real site, at which point you discover that reality is annoyingly high-resolution and doesn’t care about your VRAM budget.
The captures we actually wanted to show people were bigger than the capacity of the machines, and there was no more clever packing to be done. So the whole scene can't be resident at once. Which means only part of it can be. Which means the renderer has to decide, every frame, which part to render, go and fetch it and then draw it on-screen. Stop me if you’ve heard this before.
What LOD even means for splats
If you've done anything in real-time graphics, you know about LODs: far-away things get a cheaper stand-in. A distant tree mesh becomes a lower-poly tree, then a billboard, then a smudge. Things get cheaper over distance.
Splats don't have

hn.title: Faster than earcut: triangulating 3.7M map polygons in 489 ms
hn.text:
We have published the polygon triangulator of our map engine as a small library,
earstrip , under the ISC license, the same one
earcut uses. It is one C++ header, and a WebAssembly build on
npm that takes the same arguments as earcut. In C++ it is 14% faster than
earcut.hpp, in the browser 1.4 to 2.1 times as fast as earcut.js, and the
comparison is near the end. This post is about how we got
there.
A GPU fills triangles and nothing else. A map, on the other hand, is mostly polygons: buildings, parks, parking
lots, the strip of grass between two tram tracks. Here are a few blocks of Śródmieście in Warsaw the way our
renderer reads them from a map file, as outlines :
Outlines Triangles
Before any of this gets a fill, every outline has to be cut into
triangles . Hover over a polygon, or tap it, to see what it turns into.
These blocks hold 331 polygons with 5,151 vertices, and they become 4,514 triangles.
Zoom level 13 of our offline map of the Masovian Voivodeship, the region around Warsaw, has 3,740,425 polygons.
On one core of an M4 Pro, the constrained Delaunay triangulator in our engine needs 2.93 seconds to cut all of
them. This October I replaced it with ear clipping. To write this post I rebuilt the ear clipper one idea at a
time, one commit per idea, and timed every commit on those same 3.7 million polygons, so each section below ends
with a number.
Delaunay ​
A triangulation of a set of points is Delaunay when no point lies inside the circle through the three corners of
any triangle. Two triangles that share an edge are enough to see how the rule works. Drag the point D:
Smallest angle 45° ; with BD instead it would be 37°
While D stays outside the dashed circle through A, B and C, the shared edge is AC.
Push D into the circle and the edge flips to BD;
pull it back out and it flips back. Each flip is a local repair,
and a triangulation where no edge wants to flip is Delaunay. Of all the ways to triangulate the same points, it
has the largest smallest angle. The orange arc marks the smallest angle of the two
triangles, and the line under the figure shows what the other diagonal would give: wherever you put D, the edge
the circle rule picks wins.
"Constrained" means that the polygon's own edges must stay edges of the triangulation, even where the circle rule
would flip them away. Our triangulator inserts the vertices one at a time. For each new point it walks across the
triangles built so far until it finds the one the point falls into, splits it, and flips edges around the new
point until the circle rule holds again. It also forces the polygon's edges in, and at the end it keeps only the
triangles that lie inside the polygon and outside its holes.
Well-shaped triangles matter when you interpolate something across them or run a simulation on them. A flat fill
doesn't care: a GPU fills a needle-thin triangle as correctly as a fat one. And most of the work is spent on
polygons that hardly need any. Almost half of the Masovian polygons, 1.8 million, have four vertices or fewer.
A triangle needs no cutting at all and a convex quad is two triangles, yet the Delaunay code spends 302 ms on
them, building each triangulation from scratch.
Ears ​
An ear of a polygon is a corner you can cut off with one straight cut. Take three consecutive vertices a, b and c.
If the corner at b is convex and no other part of the polygon reaches into the triangle abc, that triangle is an
ear. Cut it off, and what remains is a polygon with one vertex fewer. In 1975 Gary Meisters proved that every
simple polygon with more than three vertices has at least two ears that don't overlap. So there is always another
ear to cut, and a polygon with n vertices falls apart into n − 2 triangles.
Here is one of the buildings from the blocks above. Move the slider
to cut its ears one at a time, or cut them all :
0 / 25
The green triangle is the next ear to go. The algorithm needs one test, "is this corner an
ear?", and the simplest version of it checks the corner and then every other vertex of the boundary. cross is
the 2×2 determinant found in every geometry codebase; it is positive when c lies to the left of the line from a
to b, so for a boundary that runs counter-clockwise a positive cross(a, b, c) means a convex corner:
static double cross ( double ax , double ay , double bx ,
double by , double cx , double cy )
{
return ( bx - ax ) * ( cy - ay ) - ( by - ay ) * ( cx - ax ) ;
}
bool isEar ( uint32_t v ) const
{
const Node & b = _nodes [ v ] ;
const Node & a = _nodes [ b . prev ] , & c = _nodes [ b . next ] ;
if ( cross ( a , b , c ) <= 0 )
return false ; // turns the wrong way, or not at all
for ( uint32_t w = c . next ; w != b . prev ;
w = _nodes [ w ] . next ) {
const Node & p = _nodes [ w ] ;
if ( cross ( a . x , a . y , b . x , b . y , p . x , p . y ) < 0 ||
cross ( b . x , b . y , c . x , c . y , p . x , p . y ) < 0 ||
cross ( c . x , c . y , a . x , a . y , p . x , p . y ) < 0 )
continue ; // outside the triangle
if ( ! samePos ( p , a ) && ! samePos ( p , b ) &&
! samePos ( p , c ) )
return false ;
}
return true ;
}
A point on an edge of the triangle counts as inside: if the ear touched the rest of the boundary, cutting it off
would leave a polygon that touches itself. The one exception is a point at exactly the position of a, b or c,
which happens where an outline meets itself at a single vertex. Holes make that common.
Holes ​
Ear clipping works on one closed boundary, and 11,345 of the Masovian polygons have holes, such as courtyards and
clearings in forests. The way to deal with them is to cut each hole open and stitch it to the outer ring with a
bridge, an edge from a vertex of the hole to a vertex of the boundary, walked once in each direction. The
boundary then runs around the outside, crosses the bridge, goes around the hole the other way and comes back.
There is no area between the two copies of the bridge, so the polygon is the same, but now it is one ring.
The bridge must not cross anything. David Eberl

hn.title: Disney Raising Prices Days After Confirming Ads Will Now Show Up on Every Tier
hn.text:
Disney+ Originals Can’t Crack the Emmys or Nielsen’s Top 20, But the Streamer Makes Sure Nobody Misses Out on Ads, Even on Premium
Twice a year, Nielsen pulls back the curtain on what America has actually been watching, and the numbers for the first-half of 2026 were revealed recently.
It is a genuinely encouraging picture for streaming overall: Stranger Things and The Pitt are duking it out at the top, shows like One Piece, Invincible and Shrinking are pulling healthy numbers and cracking the Top 20 Most-Watched Originals, and kids remain the single biggest force in the ecosystem, with Bluey outpacing Grey’s Anatomy outright. Even The Big Bang Theory is having a bit of a renaissance. Streaming, in other words, is working.
Here is the breakdown of the biggest original from each major streamer by total minutes viewed in the first half of 2026:
Netflix: Stranger Things — 23.261 billion minutes
HBO Max: The Pitt — 21.118 billion minutes
Paramount+: Landman — 12.400 billion minutes
Prime Video: The Boys — 9.597 billion minutes
Peacock: The Traitors — 7.737 billion minutes
Hulu: Paradise — 5.660 billion minutes
Apple TV+: Shrinking — 5.246 billion minutes
Disney+ is conspicuously absent from this list, as it does not have an original show in the Top 20 of Nielsen this year so far, which is worth highlighting given the streamer’s size and the fact that it has aired shows like Percy Jackson, Daredevil: Born Again , Star Wars: Maul – Shadow Lord, and Wonder Man already this year.
These are shows with real built-in audiences and brand recognition most competitors would auction organs for. None of them managed to break into Nielsen’s Top 20 Original Series chart for the half. None of them cracked the weekly Top 10 either, at any point, not even for a single week this year.
Stranger Things, at 23.261 billion minutes, remains the most-watched show in the country so far this year. The Pitt sits close behind at 21.118 billion, a remarkable number for a show only in its second season with 30 episodes, compared to Stranger Things’ 42. If every one of those minutes belonged solely to Season 2 of The Pitt, that is roughly 29.5 million complete binges of the season. Numbers that stay astonishing no matter how you slice them. Disney+ has nothing in that conversation.
Disney’s internal data via Luminate does manage to tell a story for its original shows that is marginally more flattering, but only marginally.
Daredevil: Born Again leads Disney+’s original series chart for H1 2026 with 3.6 billion minutes across its combined seasons, followed by Percy Jackson at 2.6 billion and The Mandalorian at 2.4 billion. Wonder Man pulled 1.9 billion minutes in its debut season. Star Wars: Maul — Shadow Lord landed at 1.1 billion. Andor sits at 918.1 million. The Punisher: One Last Kill at 586.2 million. The Book of Boba Fett and Loki both trail under 400 million.
Season views, the actual number of unique viewers tuning in, however, are not quite in Disney’s favour. Wonder Man scored 7 million season views, while Daredevil: Born Again Season 2 sits at just 5.8 million. Meanwhile, Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 2 only managed 5.3 million views.
These are not mass cultural phenomena. They are shows with dedicated pockets of fandom, titles that provoke enthusiasm within a specific audience and indifference beyond it.
These numbers for flagship Disney+ shows in 2026 are closer to Arrowverse shows like The Flash, which averaged 4.6 million viewers for its 23-episode seasons on The CW, broadcast television of all places, than they are to the expensive prestige shows they’re supposed to be.
It doesn’t help that Disney+ doesn’t make the kind of original content that wins at the Emmys. In fact, despite all the money at their disposal, none of their shows won a single award at the main ceremony this year.
All streaming services ask you to pay money for access to their libraries as well as the original programming they have lined up; among all of them, Disney+ is probably the least interesting streamer out there and offers very little in terms of original programming.
The already sparse original programming will likely shrink even more now to protect the brand value of Marvel and Star Wars following their box-office woes with movies like Thunderbolts, Captain America: Brave New World, and The Mandalorian (which is the least successful Star Wars movie ever).

hn.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2
hn.text:
jailbreaking the switch 2
ns2jb is a software-only jailbreak of the switch 2 for the current latest firmware 23.0.1
October 18, 2026
cs
Introduction
You can get a copy of the exploit from the ns2jb repository.
ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak for the Switch 2. It allows running arbitrary native code as any ordinary sysmodule, and as the built-in fs sysmodule. This lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO. To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2.
To demonstrate the capabilities of this jailbreak, Codex modded a Switch 2 exclusive, Mario Kart World. Thanks to my friends in Dabney House who helped me choose characters to add and playtest the game.
Watch the first gameplay video
Watch the second gameplay video
▶ 0:09 ▶ 0:05
cinnamoroll, red, and tole tole racing
Setup
The very first thing I did was set up a harness around the Switch 1 and 2 so Codex could, ideally, jailbreak the Switch 2 without me:
“set a goal to jailbreak the switch 2. make no mistakes”
Edit: Many people have been asking me if I actually used this prompt. No, it’s just a silly caption. I set a /goal for userland code execution, but that didn’t succeed. The jailbreak itself took substantial effort for ~2 weeks. The Mario Kart World, however, was entirely vibecoded in a day, and was just for fun.
The JetKVMs allow Codex to send controller inputs to the Switches over USB and receive video output over HDMI. We also need a way to press the power button—when the Switch 2 crashes, it needs a button press to restart.
That’s what the Bluetooth light switch flicker from Amazon is for. When the lever comes down, it presses the power button. Once the power button is fully pressed, the rest of the lever’s torque lifts the mechanism.
watch the power button get pressed
Getting code execution
WebKit is a popular target for console jailbreaks, so it’s unsurprising that Codex has picked it for initial code execution.
Code execution through the browser
It claims to have “native control-flow hijack” by taking advantage of a WebKit n-day loaded via a custom Wi-Fi captive portal.
We’d like to get code execution in microkernel services (or “sysmodules” on the Switch), so we can run homebrew, mod games, download saves, etc.
Unfortunately, this approach of replacing one JavaScript function object with another doesn’t generalize beyond existing functions—we’d need a new way to make arbitrary IPC calls. That looks difficult.
Why?
WebKit has execute-only memory, or XOM, so even with arbitrary memory RW, we don’t know where a gadget that could perform arbitrary IPC calls is.
Even if we did, perhaps by parsing relocation data, it’s not clear how we’d construct a signed pointer for it because of PAC.
And even if we could, with some signing gadget, it’s not clear how we’d call this pointer, since CFI type-checks most call sites.
Codex has reset the goal to complete these steps. It’s a side bet; it may succeed 1 , but let’s be real: the accessibility of WebKit and the Nintendo BBP reward have probably incentivized many before me to look here 2 .
While that runs, let’s explore other options.
Code execution through smilehax2
My idea was to target Switch 1 games, for two reasons:
They’re built by developers. It’s less likely we’ll need to deal with PAC and CFI, especially because the Switch 1 does not support PAC .
Since the Switch 1 root of trust is owned, we can decrypt the code and read it.
Maybe we can still get the upsides of the browser attack surface—orchestrating from JavaScript, using existing n-days, etc—while avoiding the downsides of WebKit mitigations by finding a Switch 1 game that embeds a browser? Something analogous to Electron, but for games, so we could pull off an exploit like this Discord RCE . I can’t disclose this approach’s findings publicly at the moment, but luckily, there are other Switch 1 games.
In particular, I’m interested in SmileBASIC . This is because it’s been pwned before, in smilehax , giving userspace code execution on the 3DS. It’s a giant C++ codebase; surely, if there was an exploitable memory corruption in the BASIC interpreter, there can be another.
Codex found a useful 32-bit integer overflow in the interpreter. When removing items from an array, the interpreter checked position + count <= array.length , but the sum could wrap and become negative. To fill the gap created by removing elements, it’s supposed to shift the remaining elements left, like so:
memmove (
backing + position * 8 , // start of the gap
backing + (position + count) * 8 , // elements after the gap
(length - position) * 8 // bytes to copy
);
Say we have a string array R of length 4, and we run REMOVE R,&H60000000,&H3FFFFFFF . position + count wraps to 0x9fffffff . As a negative signed 32-bit integer, it’s less than array.length . The multiplications by 8 also wrap, so we end up performing memmove(backing, backing - 8, 32) , pulling the previous 8 bytes into the array. The command does report an Out of memory error, but it doesn’t matter, since the copy has happened already.
This is useful because the 8 bytes preceding any array in SmileBASIC contain a pointer to the array itself! After the REMOVE , operations on R[0] will treat the array backing as if it were a string.
Since a pointer occupies what would be the length field of R[0] , the string length is enormous, and we can perform reads and writes out of bounds. We read and write to memory by copying to and from substrings of R[0] .
This was a Switch 1 game, so the SmileBASIC agent could work on the exploit on my Switch 1, while the WebKit agent worked on the Switch 2. After some time, it got ROP.
Getting sysmodule RW
Okay, now we need to compromise a more privileged process. We’re interested in ordinary sysmodules and built-in sysmodules .
Which sysmodule should we pursue? We don’t have their code, so it’s unclear which sysmodules have which privi

I've worked for a long time in the storage field during my career and ZFS is the piece of engineering I admire most in that space. I wanted a way to pay homage to it and to explore and better understand its internals. So I built Uberblok: a museum of ZFS. A deep dive into copy-on-write, txgs, vdevs, RAID-Z, snapshots, the ARC, metaslabs, the ZIL, send/receive with explanations and animated diagrams. I'm sure people here know these internals better than I do, so corrections are very welcome. I built it with my agent swarm organization, Algotitan. I hope you'll enjoy the deep dive into Uberblok as much as I do. Museum: https://uberblok.storagebits.workers.dev

hn.title: Getting ready to operate GNU Taler in Germany
hn.text:
Getting ready to operate Taler in Germany
For the past three years, the NGI Taler project has worked towards the goal
of making Taler legally available in the EU as an online payment system for
everyday use.
Today we can share that Taler Operations AG is being founded in Bochum.
The new German company is going to operate Taler in Euro,
enabling payments with Taler first in Germany, then in the Euro-zone.
The next steps towards that goal are to apply to BaFin,
Germany's financial supervisory authority,
for a licence as an e-money issuer.
This post explains why this company is needed,
what changed in the NGI TALER consortium,
and how citizens who want to see Taler succeed can help, including as investors.
Why Taler needs a regulated operator
Taler is a payment system, not a currency, but usable for any currency.
At its core, it issues bearer tokens to represent value, like coins,
and this renders Taler as electronic money which falls under EU regulation:
Any institution that issues electronic money (EMI) for Euros must be a bank or acquire a dedicated licence.
In the original plan of the NGI TALER project,
the Bochum-based GLS Bank took on the role of the e-money issuer for Taler,
and worked towards the deployment of the Taler payment system in Germany
with support from the other members of the NGI TALER consortium.
However, in January 2026 GLS made the decision to not pursue this role further,
for reasons unrelated to Taler as presented in their statement ( gls.de/taler ).
Since then, GLS and the other members of the NGI TALER consortium worked out the best way forward
to achieve the project's goal to make Taler available in the Euro-zone.
The outcome is the announcement today.
The new company Taler Operations AG will be set up
to apply for an e-money licence and take over the role
originally intended for GLS (who will remain a consortium member in a supporting role).
We regret that the original plan did not work out.
Integrating a new kind of payment system into an existing bank’s processes,
compliance framework and IT is hard, and banks have to set priorities.
We are grateful to GLS for its work in the project and for staying involved.
And we also think the new arrangement has a real advantage:
the institution operating Taler in Euro will be focused entirely on Taler,
instead of fitting it into a larger bank’s product portfolio and process constraints.
What Taler Operations AG will do
Legal status:
Taler Operations AG is a German stock corporation in formation, seated in Bochum,
and a subsidiary of Taler Systems SA (Luxembourg).
Purpose:
Operating a GNU Taler exchange in Germany, for the Euro,
so that citizens can pay with Taler
and merchants can accept it.
Reach:
After establishing legal operations in Germany,
Taler will become usable across the single market,
even if Taler Operations AG will initially only promote it in Germany.
Timing:
Operations can only begin once BaFin has granted the authorisation.
A launch date will be announced after that happens.
Next steps:
An application to BaFin for authorisation as an electronic money institution (EMI).
Securing funding via investors, see below, to become operable.
We stress that GNU Taler is and stays free software.
The licensed company operates a service;
Taler, the protocol suite, and its reference implementation GNU Taler remain open and free.
What this means for the community
The NGI TALER project continues:
development, security reviews, integrations from the open calls ,
and the Swiss deployment all go on as before.
The change concerns who will operate the Taler payment system in Euro in Germany,
but not the direction of the project.
We will report on the progress of the e-money licence application.
If you want to help,
you can tell merchants and organisations you care about that Taler is coming.
You can try the Taler wallet
with the demo site and report issues.
You can also contribute to the software .
And you can invest to help us fund the launch
and, if successful, benefit as a shareholder:
For investors
Getting an e-money licence takes capital.
The law sets minimum own funds for EMIs,
and BaFin also expects a credible business plan,
staffing, compliance and IT security before granting authorisation.
Taler Operations AG is therefore raising capital now.
We are looking for investors who:
want a privacy-preserving, free-software payment system to become legally available in Germany and the Euro area;
understand that this is a regulated infrastructure business with a licensing phase before revenue; and
are able to invest at least €50,000.
We are especially interested in investors who share the values behind Taler:
privacy for buyers, transparency for taxable income, no lock-in, and payments as public-interest infrastructure.
Contact us at
invest@taler-systems.com
to be given access to further business information.

anthropic.title: Open call for guest investigators in the life sciences
anthropic.text:
Today, we’re inviting members of the life sciences community to apply to work with us on special projects. We’re looking for proposals from principal investigators and their research groups at academic institutions, nonprofits, or government labs who want to use Claude to investigate key questions in causal human biology, structural and computational molecular biology, medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, and clinical science.
You can submit a proposal for a project here .
Over 8–12 weeks, guest investigators will work directly with Anthropic researchers on a problem of interest and produce the analyses, artifacts, and tools that will be most helpful for them in their work. Our team will run our models and harnesses at no cost to them.
We’ll work together to publish these outputs and open-source the accompanying data and code. Guest investigators retain the rights to their data at every step during their project. They will also have the rights to any independent follow-on research that might come out of our collaboration.
We’re looking for applicants who can clearly explain how they would benefit from direct collaboration with Anthropic’s researchers. Applicants should also make a reasonable case that their outputs (e.g., preliminary discoveries, answers to open questions, open-source datasets, or public resources) can be produced within the 8- to 12-week collaboration period. There may be an option for extension beyond the initial collaboration period for some projects.
We understand that the results for most open problems of interest will take much longer to validate, but we’re looking for proposals that can produce some preliminary evidence in a relatively short amount of time.
We aren’t asking for guest investigators to give us their data, either in the application or during the collaboration, and we’re requesting that applicants include only publicly available information in their application materials.
Applications will be open for approximately 14 days, and we’ll strive to notify selected participants by email approximately 14 days after applications close. We look forward to potentially expanding this effort in the future as we learn more about how we can best support the scientific community.
This program is one of several initiatives Anthropic is pursuing to invest more heavily in the life sciences and the broader scientific research community. Scientists who would like direct access to our most capable publicly available models for biology can apply to join our Life Sciences Verification Program . We’ve also continued to support researchers through our AI for Science initiative , which provides scientists with Claude credits to accelerate their progress toward making scientific discoveries.

nvidia.title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
nvidia.summary: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with […]
nvidia.text:
Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment.
The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications.
The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next.
On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI
In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy.
Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models.
Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said.
He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.”
The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems.
Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture.
Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people.
“If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.”
Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally.
Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity.
For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI.
“I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.”
The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling
The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace.
Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027.
A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships.
Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials.
“What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.”
Kazakhtelecom , the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty.
Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley , along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale.
An Honorary Black Belt for Huang
Later that day, also at the Akorda Presidential Palace, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Huang with an honorary black belt in Judo. The belt, embroidered in gold stitching, was a special thanks from President Tokayev for Huang’s support of Kazakhstan’s AI ambition and for leadership aligned with the spirit and rigor of the martial art.
At the end of their meeting President Tokayev had another honor for Huang, presenting him with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, for Huang’s contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan. Dostyk means friendship and the Order honors peace, friendship and cooperation.

nvidia.text:
Lock in and load out this GFN Thursday. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to supported devices . The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud.
There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen.
Plus, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners.
It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week.
Deployment Without the Downloads
Squad up and answer the call on the cloud.
Activision and Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory.
Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads.
Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. The DMZ extraction mode sends players into contested territory to recover valuable technology, weigh objectives and decide when to get out. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground.
Ultimate members can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. With game downloads and installs handled by GeForce NOW, members can spend less time preparing a local rig and more time preparing the next loadout.
A New Way to Play
A new way to join GeForce NOW on Fire TV.
GeForce NOW in-app purchase is rolling out to existing supported Fire TV Stick users, making it possible to purchase a membership directly through Amazon using an existing account. Transactions are processed through Amazon’s billing system, creating a more seamless path from setup to gameplay.
GeForce NOW transforms Fire TV into a powerful PC gaming rig in the cloud. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA.
The library includes thousands of ready-to-play games, including many of the world’s most-played titles and more than 100 free-to-play games. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming.
A Pixel-Perfect Fantasy
Classic roots. A new adventure.
Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world.
Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective.
Exploit enemy weaknesses to stagger foes, break their defenses and seize extra turns before finishing the bonus phase with powerful Resonance attacks. Airships, crystals, espers and moogles bring familiar series favorites to a world filled with secrets to discover.
GeForce NOW handles the game’s downloads and storage in the cloud, leaving more space on supported devices for everyday essentials. Save the inventory management for potions and Phoenix Downs.
Step Into a New Season in Tamriel
Familiar lands. Fresh reasons to return.
The Elder Scrolls Online ’s second season , Echoes of Skyrim , launched Wednesday, Oct. 21, free for all ESO players and ready to stream through GeForce NOW.
Season Two gives everyone who owns ESO Standard Edition access to its Skyrim content and the Antiquities treasure-hunting system. The Markarth downloadable content follows Monday, Nov. 9, rounding out the additions with two classic zones to explore.
The Season also introduces Solo Dungeons, reimagining challenges previously designed for groups. Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices have been redesigned and rebalanced for players ready to tackle their dangers alone. nvidia.summary: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF […]
nvidia.text:
At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure.
Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x.
“Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.”
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Training on Accelerated Infrastructure
Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data.
Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases.
SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls.
Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost
Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them.
Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer.
NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR.
Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model.
Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads.
Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research
LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.
RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends.
Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection
RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios.
HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine .
Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection.

nvidia.title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
nvidia.summary: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion […]
nvidia.text:
Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem.
Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues.
One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together:
NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground.
NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets.
NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations.
GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability.
Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready , helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories.
Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin.
Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token.
Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention.
Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope.
Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid.
Explore the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and the Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design . Learn more from NVIDIA and energy leaders who are accelerating power-flexible AI factories to strengthen the grid at GTC Berlin.
Visit Hitachi Energy (booth 7004, hall 7), Schneider Electric (booth 3041, hall 3) and Siemens Energy (booth 3048, hall 3) and tune into sessions with Schneider Electric on Wednesday, Oct. 21: From Grid to AI: Engineering the Future of AI Factories and Energy Intelligence: Powering the AI Era .

nvidia.title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
nvidia.summary: European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open […]
nvidia.text:
European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin.
Frontier Results With Open Models
Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D.
Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations.
Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes.
Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image, about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes.
Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x.
In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow.
L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing.
Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs.
Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation
NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands.
Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation .
ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara .
CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine.

nvidia.title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects
nvidia.summary: Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control. Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, […]
nvidia.text:
Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control.
Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant.
NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure.
Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications
Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its Haystack Enterprise Platform , the foundation of AI@EC, the European Commission’s shared platform for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure.
The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems.
NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis.
Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment
Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models.
Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results.
With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers.
NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow.
UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling
London-based Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK , a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities.
Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work
In Germany, Materna is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with NVIDIA Audio2Face available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure.
For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, Red Hat and deepset are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and NVIDIA Nemotron open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers.
To support local development, the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes Nemotron-Personas-Germany, an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with NeMo User Sim so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas.
France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace
CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected LINAGORA and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai.
More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment.
Greece: A Local Agentic Ecosystem
Greek AI and energy company KIEFER is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge

nvidia.text:
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark , which launched last week , powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December.
Announcements include:
Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark
DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23
NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month
October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills
DGX Station improves manageability with seven new integrations
DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses
Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station
NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station
Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware
Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models
New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware.
Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin .
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC
RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute.
Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release:
“A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag
“Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge
“An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag
Underdog , a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download .
To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader.
During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B.
ASUS , Dell Technologies , HP , Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon.
Learn more about RTX Spark , and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks .
DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build
New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23.
When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant . This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash.
Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3.
Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook .
NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance.
The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode.
DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer , ASUS , Dell Technologies , GIGABYTE , HP , Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA.
DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk
For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems.
New integrations with Absolute Security , Splunk by Cisco , Fleet Device Managemen t , Microsoft Intune , Perforce Puppet , Progress Software Chef and Tanium let IT teams manage DGX Station systems through enterprise setup, management and conformity processes, helping accelerate approvals and reduce deployment risk while minimizing time to first token.
With the upcoming Windows-based systems, developers can build workflows that harness professional applications, run on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and operate from agents that run their large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA GB300 systems — all in one machine.
DGX Station for Windows , expected from system manufacturer partners in December, extends local AI into the applications and operating environment enterprises already use. Engineers can run local models and agents in Windows-native software with access to AI models, tools and agents on the same system.
DGX Station for Windows will feature support for manufacturing applications from nTop , Dassault Systèmes , Keysight Technologies , MathWorks , Rockwell Automation , Siemens , Synops

nvidia.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
nvidia.summary: General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding […]
nvidia.text:
General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers.
A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites.
Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale.
“We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.”
WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents.
The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance.
As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own.
Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence.
To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets.
Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances.

Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. nvidia.text:
Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design.
NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do.
Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure
Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow.
As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget.
